findings.title: referenceImages is a CONTENT anchor, not a STYLE anchor -- confirmed independently, contradicts a mid-run course-correction
findings.detail: iter1: referenceImages=[crypt_dense_v1] (ARM B's proven crypt reference) reproduced a full crypt scene wholesale on the camp base twice (sarcophagus, skulls, stone pillars; registration 0.758 and 0.987 -- the 0.987 run scores well on edge-recall DESPITE wrong content, a metric-gaming false positive). iter1-2: swapping to camp_clearing_night_v2 (the SAME-ROOM incumbent) as the reference did NOT fix this -- it reproduced v2's OWN specific composition (a timber cabin + stone perimeter wall that do not exist in this greybox) across 4 separate attempts (0.644, 0.796, 0.808, 0.839-with-reinforced-anti-import-prompt), never the greybox's actual authored layout (loose 4-tree treeline, 2 boulders, campfire, 3 bedrolls, crates -- see qa/seed_gfx_camp_clearing.py). A mid-task course-correction asserted the same-room reference's content leak would be 'benign' -- this batch's own 4 real generations refute that for this greybox; the sibling forest-road lane's findings.json (qa/evidence/plate-sprint/forest-road/, worktree wt-forest-road) independently confirms both anchors leaked their full room content and does not claim a same-room exception either.
findings.fix: Drop referenceImages entirely; carry the target painterly style as TEXT ONLY in the prompt (the existing rich style description already covers oil-brush strokes / chiaroscuro / warm-cool falloff). This is the arm that actually converged content-wise.

findings.title: scene-content grounding + explicit anti-import clause was necessary once referenceImages was dropped
findings.detail: The base ControlNet pass renders camp's authored trees/boulders as blocky rectangular placeholders (matching the greybox's simple box geometry); the plain style-pass prompt read these as literal stone pillars/columns (the base template's crypt-authored boilerplate 'varied unique pillar carvings... crisply chiseled stone relief' leaking in from generate_room.py's shared prompt template, which is not room-gated). Adding explicit SCENE-CONTENT GROUNDING language ("the tall vertical shapes are TREES... the low blocky shapes are BOULDERS... NO walls/buildings/architecture") fixed this: no-ref generations correctly painted real gnarled trees and rounded mossy boulders, matching the tombstone-monolith fix already documented in room_recipes.json for the z-image pipeline (2026-07-09 camp v1->v2 audit) -- same lesson, different pipeline.

findings.title: best-of-3 control_strength sweep: 0.85 beat 0.7 and 0.92
findings.detail: Base ControlNet control_strength 0.7 (ARM B's crypt default) -> best style-pass registration 0.9005/0.9254 across iters 1-2. Raising to 0.85 (iter3) raised the best-of-3 ceiling to 0.9439 (this lane's best candidate). Raising further to 0.92 (iter4) REGRESSED to 0.8818 best-of-3 -- not a monotonic lever; 0.85 is the measured sweet spot for this room/base pair, not a universal constant.

findings.title: course-correction's suggested dimetric/camera-lock clause tested and found NOT beneficial for this base
findings.detail: A mid-run course-correction (citing the sibling forest-road lane's finding-3: dropping referenceImages also drops an implicit camera pin, recoverable via an explicit dimetric-lock prompt clause) was tested directly: added the same camera-lock wording to the winning no-ref prompt and ran best-of-3 on the identical iter3 base. Result: 0.8302 / 0.8613 / 0.6249 -- all WORSE than the plain no-ref prompt's 0.9439. Root cause: this camp base's camera projection was never drifting (unlike forest-road's base, which tilted to an eye-level landscape without a reference) -- the extra camera-lock + scene-grounding wording only added prompt complexity/stochastic risk without fixing an actual defect here. Kept the plain no-ref prompt as the winner; documented rather than silently adopting the suggested change.

findings.title: edge-recall vs greybox is content-blind and may undercount faithful organic reinterpretation (advisory, per sibling lane's finding-2)
findings.detail: The winning candidate's overlay (overlay_candidate_vs_greybox.jpg: magenta greybox structural edges composited over the candidate) shows the floor-diamond boundary, tree positions, and boulder position landing correctly on painted structure -- visually a well-registered plate. Its raw edge-recall (0.9439) sits just under the 0.95 gate, plausibly because painting an authored BOX placeholder as an organic tree trunk/canopy naturally sheds some of the box's own edge pixels (the metric was co-tuned on hard-edged crypt masonry). Reporting the number as the gate result (FAIL, per the sprint's literal bar) while flagging this class-dependent caveat, consistent with the sibling forest-road lane's own advisory framing of the same metric behavior.
